verdicts.summary: The before/after branch check compares like with like. `currentBranch` and the cached local `refName` are both the short branch name, or null when detached.
verdicts.scenario: I tried detached HEAD, an unborn branch, and a branch whose short name is also a tag name (`rev-parse --abbrev-ref` would give `heads/release`, but this path doesn't use it). Local status takes `refName` from porcelain `# branch.head`, which is null for `(detached)`. `currentBranch` runs `symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD`, exits 1 when detached (null), and strips `refs/heads/`. The two values agree in each case, so no spurious mismatch or refresh loop occurs. On a real switch, `readRemoteStatus` returns null. `updateCachedRemoteStatus` then stores `remote: null` rather than a value marker, because `undefined` never equals a branch name or null. The next poll or read therefore reloads the remote.

verdicts.summary: The remote write lock is held only for bounded work. The open question about what bounds a PR lookup is answered by the VcsProcess default timeout.
verdicts.scenario: I tried a hung `gh`/provider call holding the per-cwd lock so that `getStatus` and the full refresh queue behind it indefinitely. The source-control host runs its commands through `VcsProcess`, whose `spawn` applies `timeout: input.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s) with `timeoutBehavior: "error"`. A stuck lookup therefore errors and releases the lock. `lookupStatusPr` also catches lookup errors and falls back to the last known PR. Publishing local status before the lock cannot deadlock, because `refreshLocalStatusCore` takes no lock. I did not open the gh adapter to confirm it passes no larger `timeoutMs`.

verdicts.summary: `refreshLocalStatusCore` now runs outside the remote lock for every `refreshStatus`. Two concurrent refreshes could write local status out of order, so an older snapshot is published after a newer one.
verdicts.scenario: The web branch selector sends `refreshStatus({localOnly:true})` (BranchToolbarBranchSelector.tsx:511) while a turn-end full refresh is in flight. Both call `invalidateLocalStatus`, then `localStatus`, then `updateCachedLocalStatus`. The final write is one atomic `Ref.modify`, but its order follows read completion, not read start. If the earlier-started read finishes last, it overwrites the newer local snapshot and publishes `localUpdated` with the older value. Before this change the lock serialized `refreshStatus` calls. I did not read `localStatusResultCache` and its invalidate/in-flight semantics, so I cannot confirm this ordering is reachable. The effect would be small and self-heals on the next refresh.
